<!-- agent-pr-review:readiness round=1 -->
## Readiness review (round 1): Needs answers

**Issue:** #29 [S6-02] Real Transcriber: AudioWorklet PCM → Transcribe Streaming via Identity Pool credentials · **Read at:** 2026-10-04 21:57 UTC · **Default branch:** `main` @ `9b2c17b`

The issue asks for the production voice path: AudioWorklet capture at 16 kHz PCM, a lazy-loaded Transcribe Streaming client using Identity Pool credentials, the Identity Pool ID in the SPA's config, a live check of the role, and latency measured on four browsers. Two things need settling first. Adding `identityPoolId` to `Amplify.configure` makes the existing `getIdToken` also fetch AWS credentials, and it rejects when that fetch fails, so a voice setting could break text chat. Nothing yet says whether #29 or #36 switches the app over to the real Transcriber.

Round: 1 · Questions: 2 · Assumptions: 12 · Suggested edits: 7 · Harness version: 2026.10.04.4

**To answer:** reply on this issue with one line per item, in the form shown under each
(`Decision r1/<ID>: <answer>`): an option's letter or your own words for a question,
"accept" or "reject" for an edit, and your correction for an assumption you disagree with.
Then ask for the apply step, which writes your answers into the issue's description.

### Questions

#### Q-1: Once the Identity Pool is configured, should text chat keep working when Cognito can't issue AWS credentials?

- **Why it matters:** `getIdToken` (`apps/web/src/auth/authService.ts:115-123`) is the token getter that #36 wires into every `POST /api/chat` and `POST /api/session` call (issue #36 AC2). It calls `fetchAuthSession()`. Once `identityPoolId` is configured, Amplify also exchanges the ID token for AWS credentials on that call, and it throws if the exchange fails (installed `@aws-amplify/core` 6.19.2, `dist/esm/singleton/Auth/index.mjs`: "getCredentialsAndIdentityId will throw if cannot get credentials"). Credentials are cached for about 50 minutes and fetched again whenever the ID token changes, so the exchange runs at sign-in and roughly hourly. A Cognito Identity outage, a wrong `VITE_IDENTITY_POOL_ID`, or a dev server on the Cognito mock with the variable set would then fail typed chat as well as voice. The current `getIdToken` tests (`authService.test.ts:132-183`) run without an Identity Pool, so they won't catch this. If the agent picks the wrong option, the auth module gets reworked after #36 has wired it in.
- **Source:** the issue is silent on this. AC3 settles that `identityPoolId` goes into `Amplify.configure` (drift-audit decision 15), not whether the token path may depend on it. NFR-006 (`docs/PRD.md:128`) requires text chat in all six browsers. Voice is best effort in two of them.
- **Options:**
  - (a) Keep the token path independent: `getIdToken` reads tokens through Amplify's token provider (`Amplify.Auth.getTokens()`, the same call `fetchAuthSession` makes first, which also refreshes). Voice alone calls `fetchAuthSession()` for credentials. A test with a failing Cognito Identity endpoint shows `getIdToken` still returns the token. Scope: within the issue (`authService.ts` and its test are owned).
  - (b) Accept the coupling: `getIdToken` keeps calling `fetchAuthSession()`, and an Identity Pool failure fails chat requests as a transient error. This is less code, and the behaviour is documented in the README. Scope: within the issue.
  - (c) Keep the Identity Pool out of `Amplify.configure` and use `fromCognitoIdentityPool` from `@aws-sdk/credential-providers` for voice only. Scope: reverses AC3's wording and drift-audit decision 15.
- **Recommendation:** (a). It keeps decision 15 as written and keeps "text chat must work" (NFR-006) separate from a voice dependency. The change is a few lines in a file the issue already owns.
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/Q-1: (a)`

#### Q-2: Does #29 switch the app to the real Transcriber, or does #36?

- **Why it matters:** #36 has the criterion "Voice uses the real Transcriber (#29)" and owns `apps/web/src/chat/ChatPage.tsx`, where #28 mounts the mic (issue #28 AC7). #29's own live checks (AC4's first real stream and AC6's measurements) need a build where the mic uses the real Transcriber. If #29 builds only `transcribe/`, those runs use a local wiring that never merges, and #36 redoes it. If #29 wires it in but the selection ends up in `ChatPage.tsx`, the change falls outside #29's owned paths and overlaps #36.
- **Source:** issue #29's owned paths: "`apps/web/src/voice/**` outside `transcribe/` (only the missing-config state; call it out in the PR)". Issue #36 AC4: "Voice uses the real Transcriber (#29)." #28 isn't built yet, so where it constructs the `Transcriber` is unknown.
- **Options:**
  - (a) #29 does the switch: one factory under `apps/web/src/voice/` picks the real Transcriber when the Identity Pool ID is configured, or the missing-config behaviour otherwise, and #28's mic uses it. After #29 merges, the deployed app streams for real, and #36's criterion only checks it end to end. If #28 constructs the Transcriber in `ChatPage.tsx`, a one-line change there is called out as a shared-file change. Scope: within the issue, with E-7's wording.
  - (b) #29 delivers `transcribe/` and a factory only, and #36 switches the app over. #29's measurements run on an unmerged local wiring, described in the PR. Scope: within the issue.
- **Recommendation:** (a). Choosing real or mock by whether the ID is configured is the missing-config logic the issue already gives #29. The live runs then measure the code that ships, and #36 keeps a check rather than new wiring.
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/Q-2: (a)`

### Assumptions

The coding agent will follow these unless you correct them.

| ID | Assumption | Basis | To correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| A-1 | Transcribe credentials come from Amplify's `fetchAuthSession().credentials`. No `@aws-sdk/credential-providers` is added, so the owned-paths allowance for "a credentials provider" goes unused. Amplify builds the login map from the ID token's issuer, so the `cognito-idp.<region>.amazonaws.com/<userPoolId>` key from PR #94 comes out right without hard-coding it. | AC3 (`identityPoolId` in `Amplify.configure`); installed `@aws-amplify/auth` `providers/cognito/credentialsProvider/utils.mjs` (`formLoginsMap` uses the token's `iss`) | `Decision r1/A-1: <your correction>` |
| A-2 | `VITE_IDENTITY_POOL_ID` is optional and stays outside `resolveCognitoConfig`'s "set both or neither" rule (`apps/web/src/auth/config.ts:23-31`). A missing ID never breaks sign-in; it only takes voice off the real path. On the Cognito mock fallback the ID is ignored, because mock tokens can't be exchanged. (would have asked) | AC3: "When it's missing … voice doesn't try a real stream"; `scripts/deploy-web.sh:76-90` already refuses to build a deploy without it | `Decision r1/A-2: <your correction>` |
| A-3 | Missing-config state (AC3 leaves this to the agent): the dev server on the Cognito mock uses the MockTranscriber, kept out of production builds the way `main.tsx:14-18` drops the mock API. Any other build without the ID shows the mic disabled with a one-line explanation rather than hiding it, so FR-020's "Mic button next to the text input" (`docs/PRD.md:73`) still holds. Listed in the PR. | AC3 "agent decides; list in the PR"; FR-020 | `Decision r1/A-3: <your correction>` |
| A-4 | The Transcribe client's region comes from the Identity Pool ID's prefix (`us-east-1:…`), as Amplify does for Cognito Identity. No `VITE_REGION` is added. | CLAUDE.md "Region: `us-east-1`"; `deploy-web.sh:100` passes no region | `Decision r1/A-4: <your correction>` |
| A-5 | `@aws-sdk/client-transcribe-streaming` is loaded with a dynamic `import()` the first time the mic is used. `apps/web/build.test.ts` checks that the entry chunk `index.html` references doesn't contain it and that another chunk does. | ADR-006:53 "We lazy-load it only when the mic is first used"; build harness `build.test.ts:22-45` | `Decision r1/A-5: <your correction>` |
| A-6 | Capture starts when recording starts, and chunks are held until the WebSocket opens, so the first words aren't lost. Chunks are 1600 samples (3200 bytes, 100 ms); anything in ADR-006's 50-200 ms range is acceptable. Downsampling and s16le encoding are a pure module, unit-tested in jsdom, and the worklet is thin. The worklet goes in `public/worklets/` or `src/` via a Vite URL import, whichever keeps `npm run lint` and `typecheck` green. Any `eslint.config.js` change is called out as a shared-file change. | ADR-006:14, :42; `eslint.config.js:22-36` gives non-TS files Node globals only | `Decision r1/A-6: <your correction>` |
| A-7 | Stream parameters: `en-US`, `pcm`, 16000 Hz, PII redaction off, no custom vocabulary, no partial-results stabilization unless #10 recommends it. Partials aren't shown. The transcript is the first alternative of each `IsPartial: false` result in order, joined with spaces and trimmed. A stream with no final result gives an empty transcript, which #28 shows as FR-023's "I didn't catch that". | ADR-006:42, :47-48; FR-023 (`docs/PRD.md:76`) | `Decision r1/A-7: <your correction>` |
| A-8 | Errors (credentials, WebSocket close, Transcribe exceptions, mic track ended) are reported through #28's `Transcriber` interface, and #28's overlay shows FR-024's retry / type-instead. The stream is never retried automatically. #28's overlay owns the 10 s timer, and the real Transcriber closes its stream when the overlay gives up or cancels (see E-3). | FR-024 (`docs/PRD.md:77`) makes retry the patient's action; issue #28 AC5 owns the timer | `Decision r1/A-8: <your correction>` |
| A-9 | Cancel, Esc, unmount and sign-out close the WebSocket and discard everything. The mic track and AudioContext are released after each recording, so the browser's mic indicator turns off. No audio is stored. | ADR-006:45 "Close the stream and discard everything"; ADR-004/ADR-009 (no audio stored) | `Decision r1/A-9: <your correction>` |
| A-10 | AC4 runs once, with a signed-in demo user, on the env used for AC6. If the stream is denied, the agent doesn't change `infra/stacks/auth.yaml` or the bootstrap boundary. It reports the denial first and files an issue (see E-6). | CLAUDE.md AWS rules (ask before touching bootstrap); `.claude/agents/task-worker.md` (steps the worker can't run go first in its report) | `Decision r1/A-10: <your correction>` |
| A-11 | Measurement setup: timing comes from `performance.now()` at Send and at the last final result, logged in dev builds only, never shown in production. Runs use an ephemeral env (`scripts/deploy.sh all <name>`, then `scripts/deploy-web.sh <name>` with seeded users), as `deploy-web.sh:62-65` advises for unmerged branches. Publishing the branch over shared `dev` happens only after asking Nick. iOS Safari and Android Chrome need Nick's devices, so the agent lists those runs first in its report. (would have asked) | NFR-006 (`docs/PRD.md:128`); getUserMedia needs HTTPS on phones; `task-worker.md` | `Decision r1/A-11: <your correction>` |
| A-12 | Docs: the `src/voice/` row of `apps/web/README.md:20` and the config line at `:29` are updated for S6-02 and the third ID. A journal entry records the choices the issue leaves to the agent (see E-5 for the path). The 2026-10-03 journal line saying "#28 (voice) adds the Identity Pool" stays as dated history. `scripts/deploy-web.sh` isn't changed, though its bundle check greps only for the user pool ID (`:107-111`); a matching Identity Pool check would be a follow-up issue. | CLAUDE.md definition of done (journal for decisions the spec left open); journal entries are dated records | `Decision r1/A-12: <your correction>` |

### Suggested edits to the issue

#### E-1: Say the deploy script part of AC3 is already done, so the agent doesn't touch `scripts/`

Before:
```text
#100's `scripts/deploy-web.sh` passes it from SSM and fails without it, so a deployed build always has it.
```
After:
```text
`scripts/deploy-web.sh` (#100, merged) already passes it from SSM and fails without it (`scripts/deploy-web.sh:76-100`), so a deployed build always has it; #29 doesn't change the script.
```
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/E-1: accept` (or `reject`)

#### E-2: Make AC4's "and nothing else" checkable

Before:
```text
- [ ] The first real stream verifies that the Identity Pool role allows `transcribe:StartStreamTranscriptionWebSocket` and nothing else (PR #94: the permission "hasn't been exercised yet; #29's first real stream does that"); result in the PR.
```
After:
```text
- [ ] The first real stream verifies that the Identity Pool role allows `transcribe:StartStreamTranscriptionWebSocket` (a stream with a signed-in demo user's Identity Pool credentials returns a transcript) and nothing else (the role's only policy lists that one action, and one other call with the same credentials, such as `transcribe:ListTranscriptionJobs`, is denied) (PR #94: the permission "hasn't been exercised yet; #29's first real stream does that"); result in the PR, with no credentials or account IDs in it.
```
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/E-2: accept` (or `reject`)

#### E-3: Say who owns errors, Cancel and the 10 s timeout in AC5 (#28 already owns the timer)

Before:
```text
- [ ] Stream starts on record, ends on Send; waits for final results; handles errors with retry/type-instead. If no final transcript arrives within 10 s of Send, it shows the FR-024 error (drift-audit decision 4).
```
After:
```text
- [ ] Stream starts on record, ends on Send; waits for final results. Cancel closes the stream and discards everything (ADR-006). Errors (credentials, WebSocket, Transcribe exceptions, the mic track ending) reach #28's overlay through the `Transcriber` interface, which shows the FR-024 retry / type-instead; the stream is never retried automatically. The 10 s FR-024 timeout after Send is #28's overlay timer (drift-audit decision 4); the real Transcriber closes its stream when the overlay gives up, tested with a fake Transcribe client that never returns a final result.
```
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/E-3: accept` (or `reject`)

#### E-4: Define AC6's measurement, and what happens when a browser misses

Before:
```text
- [ ] Stop→final p95 ≤ 2 s measured on Chrome (desktop), Safari (macOS), iOS Safari and Android Chrome; Firefox and Edge are best effort (drift-audit decision 4, NFR-006); results in PR
```
After:
```text
- [ ] Stop→final p95 ≤ 2 s (from Send, or the 60 s auto-send, to the last final result) measured on Chrome (desktop), Safari (macOS), iOS Safari and Android Chrome over at least 20 utterances each, mixing ~5 s, 20 s and 60 s clips as in #10; Firefox and Edge are best effort (drift-audit decision 4, NFR-006); results in PR. A browser that misses 2 s is reported with its numbers and gets a follow-up issue; it doesn't block this PR.
```
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/E-4: accept` (or `reject`)

#### E-5: Own the auth files a credentials getter touches, and the journal

Adding a credentials method to `AuthService` breaks the fake in `apps/web/src/auth/testing.ts:21-44` until that file is updated too. Exposing the method beside `getIdToken` goes through `session.ts:28-30` and the barrel `index.ts:9`. The definition of done asks for a journal entry, and `docs/journal/**` isn't owned.

Before:
```text
- `apps/web/src/auth/authService.ts`, `apps/web/src/auth/authService.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/auth/config.ts`, `apps/web/src/auth/config.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/auth/env.d.ts` (the Identity Pool ID)
```
After:
```text
- `apps/web/src/auth/authService.ts`, `apps/web/src/auth/authService.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/auth/config.ts`, `apps/web/src/auth/config.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/auth/env.d.ts` (the Identity Pool ID)
- `apps/web/src/auth/session.ts`, `apps/web/src/auth/session.test.ts`, `apps/web/src/auth/index.ts`, `apps/web/src/auth/testing.ts` (a credentials getter beside `getIdToken`, and the fake `AuthService` that implements it)
- `docs/journal/**` (an entry for the choices this issue leaves to the agent)
```
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/E-5: accept` (or `reject`)

#### E-6: Add non-goals, so a failed check doesn't pull in infra or a batch fallback

Add this section after "Owned paths".

Before:
```text
```
After:
```text
## Non-goals
- No batch-transcription fallback (ADR-006 "Revisit if"); a browser that misses the latency target gets a follow-up issue.
- No change to `infra/stacks/auth.yaml`, the bootstrap permissions boundary or `scripts/deploy-web.sh`; if the role check fails, report it and file an issue.
- No live captions of partial results (ADR-006: partial results are buffered).
```
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/E-6: accept` (or `reject`)

#### E-7: Cover the real/mock choice in the `voice/` owned path (only with Q-2 (a))

Before:
```text
- `apps/web/src/voice/**` outside `transcribe/` (only the missing-config state; call it out in the PR)
```
After:
```text
- `apps/web/src/voice/**` outside `transcribe/` (choosing the real or mock Transcriber, and the missing-config state; call it out in the PR)
```
- **Reply:** `Decision r1/E-7: accept` (or `reject`)

### Reuse, dependencies and risks

- **Reuse:**
  - `resolveCognitoConfig` and `CognitoEnv` (`apps/web/src/auth/config.ts:13-31`): read the third ID the same way. `session.ts:14-19` already passes all of `import.meta.env`, so no `session.ts` change is needed just to read it.
  - The single `Amplify.configure` call (`apps/web/src/auth/authService.ts:68-75`).
  - Amplify's `fetchAuthSession().credentials` for the Transcribe client, and `Amplify.Auth.getTokens()` for a token-only path (Q-1 (a)).
  - The dynamic-import pattern in `apps/web/src/main.tsx:14-18`.
  - The build harness and forbidden-string scan in `apps/web/build.test.ts:22-45`, `:60-79`.
  - The env-stub test pattern in `apps/web/src/auth/session.test.ts:25-53`.
  - MSW with `onUnhandledFrame: "error"` (`apps/web/src/test/setup.ts:13`): any test that would open a real WebSocket fails loudly.
  - `globals.audioWorklet` from the root `globals` dependency, if a worklet lint block is added.
- **Dependencies:**
  - **#28** (Voice UI, the `Transcriber` interface, MockTranscriber): open, `status:ready`, no PR. This is the hard blocker, because the interface and overlay #29 plugs into don't exist yet (`apps/web/src/voice/` is absent).
  - **#10** (spike S-3): open. ADR-006 is still "Proposed. Pending spike S-3" (`docs/adr/0006-voice-transcription.md:3`). If the spike chooses the batch fallback for iOS Safari (ADR-006:55), revisit AC1, AC5 and AC6 before starting.
  - **#12** (PR #94), **#24/#25** (PR #120) and **#100**: closed. The Identity Pool and its Transcribe-only role are on main (`infra/stacks/auth.yaml:78-156`; the action is at `:117`), and so is the deploy wiring (`scripts/deploy-web.sh:76-100`).
  - **#36**: downstream (see Q-2).
- **Overlaps:** the code scout found no open PRs (not rechecked here). Future collisions: #28 on `apps/web/src/voice/**` and `apps/web/README.md`, and #36 on `apps/web/src/chat/ChatPage.tsx`. #29 starts after #28 merges.
- **Size:** about 800-1,300 changed lines excluding the lockfile, plus manual work: a live role check, and latency runs on four browsers, two of them on Nick's phones. It fits one PR. If you want progress before #28 and #10 land, AC3 plus the credentials getter (with Q-1 settled) could ship first as a small PR. Without a consumer it has no user-visible effect.
- **Risks:**
  - The browser build of `@aws-sdk/client-transcribe-streaming` has to sign `StartStreamTranscriptionWebSocket`, the only action the role allows. If it signs the HTTP/2 `StartStreamTranscription` instead, AC4 fails at the first stream (not verified; #10 should show it).
  - A worklet in `public/` is unhashed and outside typecheck (`apps/web/tsconfig.json` includes only `src`).
  - jsdom has no `AudioContext` or `getUserMedia`, so the Transcriber needs injected seams for the audio source and the client's `send`.

<details>
<summary>What was checked</summary>

**Requirements and testability**

- R-1 (AC1) AudioWorklet downsampling to 16 kHz s16le, ~100 ms chunks: testable for a pure downsample/encode module; "~100 ms" is fixed by A-6.
- R-2 (AC2) Lazy-loaded Transcribe client: testable in `build.test.ts` (A-5).
- R-3 (AC2) Identity Pool credentials from the ID token, with the PR #94 login key: testable against a mocked Cognito Identity endpoint; only a live run shows real credentials. The login key is derived by Amplify (A-1).
- R-4 (AC3) `identityPoolId` in `Amplify.configure`: testable. Its side effect on `getIdToken` is Q-1.
- R-5 (AC3) `VITE_IDENTITY_POOL_ID` in `config.ts` and `.env.example`: testable. The rule for a missing ID is A-2.
- R-6 (AC3) deploy-web passes and requires the ID: already on main (`deploy-web.sh:76`, `:80-90`, `:100`), so this is context, not work (E-1).
- R-7 (AC3) Missing-config state: testable ("no Transcribe client load or network call when the ID is unset"). The choice is left to the agent (A-3).
- R-8 (AC4) Role allows the one action and nothing else: manual evidence. "Nothing else" is made checkable by E-2.
- R-9 (AC5) Starts on record, ends on Send, waits for finals: testable with a fake client.
- R-10 (AC5) Retry / type-instead: untestable as written until ownership is stated (E-3, A-8).
- R-11 (AC5) 10 s timeout: duplicates issue #28 AC5; ownership is fixed by E-3.
- R-12 (AC6) p95 ≤ 2 s on four browsers: manual, and untestable as written (no sample size, no definition of stop or final, no rule for a miss). E-4 and A-11 cover it.
- R-13 (owned paths) Where the real Transcriber is wired in: Q-2, E-7.
- R-14 (goal) "per … the S-3 spike findings": depends on #10, which hasn't run.

**Analyst claims re-checked**

- `config.ts:23-31`, `authService.ts:68-75` and `:115-123`, `session.ts:13-30`, `index.ts:9`, `testing.ts:21-44`.
- `deploy-web.sh:62-65`, `:76-100` and `:107-111`.
- `auth.yaml:93-121` (the role) and `:151-156` (the SSM parameter).
- `build.test.ts:60-79`, `setup.ts:13`, `main.tsx:14-18`, `eslint.config.js:22-36`.
- `apps/web/README.md:20`, `:29`, and `.env.example`.
- ADR-006 in full, the ADR-005 amendment at line 51, and PRD lines 73-77, 124, 128 and 164.
- Issues #28, #10 and #36, and the hand-off text of PR #94 (line 65) and PR #120 (lines 222, 248).
- Amplify behaviour, read in the main checkout's installed packages (`@aws-amplify/core` 6.19.2 `singleton/Auth/index.mjs`, and `@aws-amplify/auth` `credentialsProvider.mjs` and `utils.mjs`). `fetchAuthSession` throws when the credentials fetch fails, credentials are cached for 50 minutes and cleared on token change, the login map comes from the token's `iss`, and `getTokens` is public on `Amplify.Auth`.

**Dropped**

- The region of the login key (OB-5, C-3): Amplify derives it from the token, so it's moot.
- A CSP blocking `wss://` or `cognito-identity`: `infra/stacks/web.yaml:114` uses only the managed security-headers policy, which sets no CSP.
- The stale journal line about #28: it's dated history, noted in A-12.
- When to prefetch credentials (OB-6): this is covered by buffering in A-6.

**Not checked**

- Drift-audit decisions 4 and 15 on issue #123: not in the inputs. Their effects were read through PRD 73-77 and 128, ADR-005:51, and the issue texts.
- #28's `Transcriber` interface: not written yet.
- Which action the browser Transcribe SDK signs: not installed.
- Live AWS state: no credentials used.
- The current list of open PRs on GitHub: taken from the code scout.

</details>

Decision r1/E-2: accept

## Readiness review (round 1): answers applied

**Applied** from Nick's answers (https://github.com/nick-delgado/serverless-ai-scheduling/issues/29#issuecomment-5985126356) to the [round 1 review](https://github.com/nick-delgado/serverless-ai-scheduling/issues/29#issuecomment-5984846557).

**Answers, recorded under "Decisions and clarifications":**
- **Q-1 (a):** keep the token path independent. `getIdToken` reads tokens without needing AWS credentials, so text chat keeps working when Cognito can't issue them. Voice alone depends on the Identity Pool.
- **Q-2 (a):** #29 does the switch. One factory under `apps/web/src/voice/` picks the real Transcriber when the Identity Pool ID is configured, and the missing-config behaviour otherwise.

**Edits made to the description:**
- **E-1 to E-5 and E-7:** each "Before" text was found once and replaced.
  - E-1: AC3's deploy-script part is marked done.
  - E-2: AC4's role check can now be checked.
  - E-3: AC5 says who owns errors, Cancel and the 10 s timeout.
  - E-4: AC6's measurement is defined, including what happens when a browser misses the target.
  - E-5: owned paths gain the auth files and the journal.
  - E-7: the `voice/` owned path covers the real-or-mock choice.
- **E-6:** its "Before" was empty, and the edit says "Add this section after Owned paths". The Non-goals section is inserted there, just before Dependencies.

**Edits not made:** none.

**Assumptions:** none corrected. All 12 (A-1 to A-12) are recorded as assumed.

**Questions still unanswered:** none.

Note from #28 (PR #154, owner decision `04f8fc4/SPEC-3` (a)): `Transcriber.start()` callbacks keep `onLevel` optional for an implementation. When no level arrives, the recording overlay's level dot pulses (a CSS animation that the global reduced-motion rule stops) until the first `onLevel` call. The real Transcriber here may report levels but doesn't have to.

Description repaired by hand on 2026-10-08, per the review-harness maintainers' note for 2026.10.08 (issues applied under an earlier harness version that haven't started yet). Round 1 was applied under harness 2026.10.04.4, which didn't carry the review's Reuse pointers into the description. They are now the last entry under "Decisions and clarifications" ("r1, reuse"), copied word for word from the [readiness review](https://github.com/nick-delgado/serverless-ai-scheduling/issues/29#issuecomment-5984846557). Checked as well:
